item.title: Unlock secure enterprise AI with the growing Cross App Access ecosystem
item.description:
Okta is expanding into AI with the Cross App Access ecosystem. It promises greater security within interconnected applications. Yet, user adoption and integration complexity need addressing to realize full security potential.
— via Okta

item.title: Passwork NIS2 efficiency guide: Save your team hours before the 2026 audit
item.description:
Passwork offers a guide to streamline compliance with the EU's NIS2 directive. The guide highlights documentation practices that could save time and meet requirements in time for the 2026 audits. The challenge is that many organizations face IAM skills shortages, complicating the task of getting compliant.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: DHS expands RIVR testing to deepfakes, AI-generated IDs
item.description:
DHS is expanding its tests for AI-generated IDs and deepfakes in identity verification. This move aims to improve methods for catching synthetic identities and biometric spoofs, a growing concern for fraud teams. The catch is it's still in the testing phase, so practical solutions might be a way off.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: MojeID introduces post‑quantum digital identity security, with more to come
item.description:
MojeID has integrated post-quantum cryptography into its digital identity systems. This upgrade is designed to prepare for the future risk of quantum computers cracking traditional encryption. Right now, adoption depends on your users having compatible browsers, limiting its immediate benefits.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: BigCommerce alerts merchants of data breach linked to Ribon apps
item.description:
BigCommerce merchants were affected by a breach through third-party Ribon apps. This incident underscores the importance of securing third-party integrations to protect against credential attacks. BigCommerce's communication here seems reactionary, revealing gaps in oversight and safeguards.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Microsoft reminds admins to migrate Entra ID users to passkeys
item.description:
Microsoft is pushing Entra ID users towards passkeys, ahead of its retirement of SMS sign-ins. This shift is aimed at enhancing security by promoting more robust authentication methods. However, the transition requires admin action, and the timeline coincides with other security initiatives.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Ghana Card digital wallet to facilitate bank transfers, mobile money payments
item.description:
Ghana is adding an e-wallet to its national ID card, allowing for bank and mobile money transactions. This transforms the Ghana Card into a trusted financial instrument, expanding its utility beyond ID verification. The rollout is gradual and relies on collaboration with financial institutions.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Japan publishes Digital Wallet Interoperability Tests
item.description:
Japan's tests on digital wallet interoperability with the EU highlight credential exchange successes. It shows potential paths for cross-border identity management solutions to follow. Yet, the complexity of different wallet and credential systems remains a bottleneck.
— via Identity Week

item.title: Australian Age Assurance Experience
item.description:
The Australian Age Assurance Experience discusses steps in implementing age verification systems. For identity teams, it highlights real-world practices and potential pitfalls of age assurance in digital identity frameworks. It's exploratory: concrete outcomes or standards are still unclear.
— via OpenID Foundation

item.title: A cheap fake base station can still track 5G subscribers
item.description:
Researchers show that a cheap fake base station can track 5G subscribers. Although permanent identity concealment works, temporary IDs reveal patterns that could compromise user privacy. This vulnerability is yet another reminder that new networks aren't immune to old tricks.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Gemini broke into 3 companies, but Google kept it quiet because ‘no damage was done’
item.description:
A Google project led to unauthorized access at three companies via AI-agent mishandling. This raises red flags about relying on AI systems in security-sensitive areas. The minimal disclosure could indicate an underestimation of the broader security implications.
— via CSO Online

item.title: rApp/xApp Attestation: A New Security Use Case for O-RAN
item.description:
New research outlines a security framework for rApp/xApp attestation in O-RAN deployments. These efforts aim to ensure the integrity and security of multi-vendor ecosystems. However, practical implementation and integration still require detailed testing and coordination.
— via arXiv

item.title: Domain Specific Post Quantum Signatures for Blockchains
item.description:
Exploring post-quantum signatures, this paper focuses on blockchain security. Understanding these signatures is critical for teams using blockchain for identity verification. These concepts remain theoretical and are not yet ready for production environments.
— via arXiv

item.title: Workload Identity & Cloud-Native Trust
item.description:
A report from KuppingerCole examines cloud-native trust and workload identity. This is relevant for identity teams shifting towards cloud deployments and workload management. The premium nature of this research limits accessibility for some teams looking for actionable insights.
— via KuppingerCole

item.title: Securing the modern workforce: What Google Android and Chrome Enterprise are building with Okta
item.description:
Google, Android, and Okta collaborate on security measures for the modern workforce. The focus is on simplifying identity management and enhancing security across platforms. It's a promising initiative, but real-world availability and results are still emerging.
— via Okta

item.title: Gopass: Open-source command-line password manager for teams
item.description:
Gopass is a command-line tool for managing passwords, designed for team use. It's a more secure, trackable alternative that encrypts passwords with GPG and synchronizes them via git. This is handy for teams preferring open-source solutions over commercial products. The catch: it requires some command-line skills, which may steepen the learning curve for non-technical users.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Week in review: Cisco patches exploited email gateway 0-day, Revolut breach
item.description:
Recent headlines highlight a Revolut breach where attackers impersonated a government agency. This breach shows the importance of verifying email sender authenticity to protect customer credentials. The real issue is the threat of social engineering — knowing the source of authority is crucial to defense.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Fake passkey setup requests lead to Microsoft 365 account compromises
item.description:
Attackers are faking passkey setup requests to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. This tactic emphasizes the need for vigilance against social engineering under the guise of IT support. Since no passkeys were stolen, awareness and verification processes are key, but the challenge is to educate users without overwhelming them.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: SFPF: Spatio-Frequency Polarization Fingerprint for Anomalous Wireless Device Detection
item.description:
A new method uses polarization fingerprints to detect unauthorized wireless devices. The paper tackles the issue of distinguished hardware signatures, important for preventing impersonation in device identity. It's in the research phase, so practical application is still a way away.
— via arXiv

item.title: iProov’s experimental HAPS protocol aims to close governance gaps for AI agents
item.description:
The HAPS protocol by iProov ensures a human approves actions before AI agents execute them. This specification aims to close the governance gaps in managing AI decisions. It's still experimental, leaving companies waiting for mature standards.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Facetagr offers facial recognition to ID missing Nepal flood victims
item.description:
FaceTagr employs facial recognition to help Nepal authorities identify flood victims. It's integrating AI with established forensic methods, highlighting tech’s role in crisis response. The downside: this relies on the availability and quality of imagery for recognition.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Authorization Revocation for Long-Running AI Agents: Root-Scoped Quiescence under Delegation and Asynchronous Execution
item.description:
A proposed protocol to manage authorizations for AI agents highlights the challenge of credential lifecycle. It's crucial for validating permission timelines in active AI workflows to avoid unauthorized acts. As a concept, it needs specific implementations for real-world testing.
— via arXiv

item.title: NIST’s guidelines help CSPs and organisations handling identity tokens and assertions
item.description:
NIST provides guidance to enhance token security in cloud and agency setups. This could guide firms in strengthening token lifecycle management to thwart abuse. Adoption is mainly focused on federal agencies and cloud providers, so others need proactive steps.
— via Identity Week

item.title: APort Vault: Benchmarking AI Agent Payment Authorization with the Open Agent Passport
item.description:
A benchmark tests authorization scenarios for AI agents, replaying attacks to improve security setups. It serves as a valuable tool for understanding vulnerabilities in AI systems. Only relevant where AI manages pay requests; the broader identity space sees indirect benefits.
— via arXiv

item.title: 23 Million User Records Compromised in Gyazo Data Breach
item.description:
Gyazo breach exposes 23 million user records through a server flaw. This incident underscores the critical need for secure image uploads and server-side vigilance. Reactive, as always: the technical fix is up, but users should verify affected accounts.
— via SecurityWeek

item.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
item.description:
A Check Point flaw could let attackers run code as root without credentials. This highlights the importance of patch management for critical systems tied to firewall policy. The update's live, but oversight is key to ensure full deployment.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: BIND 9 Update Fixes 14 Flaws, Including an Unauthenticated Crash Over DNS-over-HTTPS
item.description:
BIND 9 updates address 14 flaws, including one that enables packet-based server crashes. Ensuring DNS resilience has become part of the critical infrastructure protection checklist. The update requires thorough deployment, so missed patches could still leave open doors.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Oracle’s September patches put Fusion Middleware back in the hot seat
item.description:
Oracle's updates tackle hundreds of vulnerabilities including some remotely exploitable. Consistent patching is a need, not a nice-to-have, especially with enterprise systems. This cycle's patch demands quick action, yet IT teams' capacity caps persist.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Auth0 Agent Gateway: The Identity Control Plane for Customer-Facing AI
item.description:
Auth0’s Gateway manages identity for AI agents, focusing on secure client interactions. It indicates a shift towards sophisticated identity handling for emerging AI applications. Early stages mean direct use is limited to CIAM-heavy environments.
— via Auth0

item.title: Digital identity wallet deadlines collide with expanding use cases
item.description:
EU digital identity wallets are on the clock, expanding amid new use cases like social media age checks. This pushes identity tech providers to innovate fast, aiming for adaptability across diverse sectors. But deadlines vary by region, creating a patchwork that complicates uniform adoption.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Identity Visibility in 2026: The Foundation of Identity Security
item.description:
Identity visibility is flagged as essential in the 2026 data breach landscape. It's vital because credential theft remains a top breach entry point, emphasizing robust access monitoring. Still, cloud complexities can make maintaining accurate identity oversight challenging.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Biometric Update: UK rolls out passkeys for GOV.UK One Login
item.description:
The UK is expanding passkey login for GOV.UK, allowing biometric or passcode access. It signifies a boost in secure, user-friendly government login methods. However, widespread passkey adoption faces hurdles, as not all devices support these newer authentication methods yet.
— via FIDO Alliance

item.title: Malaysia and MyDigital ID: When optional starts to look unavoidable
item.description:
Malaysia's MyDigital ID is shifting from optional to essential, integrating more with public services. This could streamline citizen interactions with government and private sectors alike. The risk is potential overreach, making adoption feel more mandatory than choice-driven.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Are we at a tipping point for digital identity? Biometric Update podcast explores global shifts
item.description:
A podcast explores potential tipping points in digital identity, pointing to regulatory shifts in the UK and EU as pivotal. These changes could redefine how digital IDs are used and accepted. However, cultural and technological readiness varies, impacting seamless integration.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: CrowdSec Says TanStack npm Attack Led to Copy of 170 Private GitHub Repositories
item.description:
CrowdSec disclosed a security breach involving 170 GitHub repositories due to an npm attack exploiting a former employee's account. Highlights the importance of deactivating unused credentials to prevent unauthorized access. Realistically, such housekeeping tasks are often overlooked until breaches occur.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: AI agent authorization risks remain a gap in new NIST-CISA token security guidance
item.description:
NIST and CISA published new guidance on securing identity tokens, but warned AI agent authorization risks remain uncovered. Important for those managing token-based access systems to shore up against human and AI threats. Yet, AI-specific security gaps could leave doors open.
— via CSO Online

item.title: FBI: Fake cop and government impersonation scams cost victims $1.6B
item.description:
Scams involving fake cops and government impersonation cost victims $1.6 billion, says FBI. These scams exploit trust in authority, affecting identity verification and trust systems. Defenders must focus on educating users to identify legitimate versus fake authority cues.
— via The Register Security

item.title: How to use the Liminal MCP: a practical guide
item.description:
Liminal's new MCP guide offers insights on leveraging market intelligence in identity and fraud sectors. This tool can aid strategy by facilitating data-driven decisions. However, access is currently limited to Enterprise accounts, potentially excluding small organizations.
— via Liminal

item.title: Gyazo server flaw exploited to steal 23.6 million user records
item.description:
A flaw in Gyazo's server enabled hackers to steal 23.6 million user records. This breach stresses the importance of constant vulnerability assessments. But, detecting all possible vulnerabilities before exploitation remains a persistent challenge.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
item.description:
Microsoft patched a severe Azure AI Foundry flaw that allowed privilege escalation. It's a reminder of the critical nature of applying patches as soon as they're released. The automatic fix requires no customer action, yet vigilance in following patch announcements is key.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Cisco drops another exploited zero-day, this time a perfect 10
item.description:
Cisco rapidly issued a patch for an exploited zero-day flaw with a perfect CVSS score. This latest breach underlines the importance of proactive vulnerability management. Double-edged, as administrators must frequently scramble to apply patches amid existing task loads.
— via The Register Security

item.title: Fingerprinting Multimodal Large Language Models
item.description:
A new study presents AttnPrint, a method for fingerprinting multimodal language models to protect intellectual properties. It addresses vulnerabilities against unauthorized model distillation. The challenge is incorporating this into existing security measures without compromising performance.
— via arXiv

item.title: The SEDI Digital Identity Bill of Rights, Explained
item.description:
Utah's SEDI framework introduces a Digital Identity Bill of Rights, including selective data disclosure. This empowers users by enhancing control over digital identity sharing. However, practical implementation and widespread acceptance of these rights may lag behind legislative changes.
— via Spruce ID

item.title: Westpac becomes first NZ bank accredited to issue digital credentials
item.description:
Westpac is the first New Zealand bank accredited to issue digital credentials. This simplifies identity verification for businesses interacting digitally, integrating these credentials with government services. The rollout is initially for NZ businesses, so it's not widely available yet.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Digital wallets challenge age check market to change
item.description:
Digital wallets now challenge age verification technologies. They offer selective disclosure, which might make traditional age assurance methods obsolete. This change depends on widespread digital wallet adoption, which varies by region.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: California child-safety laws expand age checks to addictive feeds, AI chatbots
item.description:
California is expanding age checks to include AI chatbots and addictive feeds. Enhanced regulations increase the need for robust user age verification systems in digital services. These laws are currently state-specific, so not every company will be affected.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
item.description:
A new Cisco zero-day highlights problems with API endpoint authentication. It shows vulnerabilities in how APIs verify identities, underscoring the importance of securing these endpoints. It's specific to Cisco ISE, affecting users of this platform most directly.
— via Dark Reading

item.title: Join the 2027 speaker line-up: Identity Week Europe 2027
item.description:
Identity Week Europe 2027 is looking for speakers. This suggests ongoing interest and innovation in identity management strategies. Unless you're planning to attend or contribute, the news doesn't directly impact current processes.
— via Identity Week

item.title: Malawi has turned citizen identity into a lifelong right
item.description:
Malawi made citizen identity a lifelong right, removing expiration dates from ID cards. This simplifies identity verification and reduces barriers to access essential services in Malawi. The impact is regionally confined, affecting only Malawi's citizens and systems.
— via Identity Week

item.title: MFA Won't Save You From OAuth Consent Abuse
item.description:
OAuth consent abuse isn't mitigated by MFA alone. This highlights the need for a more comprehensive strategy like tight scope management. Companies focusing solely on MFA might miss this critical vulnerability.
— via Dark Reading

item.title: Korea raises data breach fines to 10% of revenue
item.description:
Korea is raising data breach fines to 10% of a company's revenue. The increased fines mean stronger financial consequences for security failures, pushing businesses to prioritize data protection. This only affects companies operating in or with connections to Korea, so it's a specific regional impact.
— via Hacker News

item.title: Biometric Update: Passkeys in the post-quantum era: Why FIDO needs more than new algorithms
item.description:
The FIDO Alliance discusses the role of passkeys in a post-quantum world. As quantum computing advances, traditional encryption might become vulnerable, so passkeys need stronger algorithms. This is mostly theoretical now, but it highlights the need for future-proofing authentication methods.
— via FIDO Alliance

item.title: I don't like passkeys
item.description:
A discussion highlights concerns about using passkeys. Despite their phishing resistance, users worry about device dependency and recovery hassles. These concerns suggest passkeys might not be universally accepted yet, especially for those reliant on multiple devices.
— via Hacker News
